author: WP08
summary: Although filed under an old fixed-function title, the unit at this revision describes the five current EasyGL profiles: what the family shares, how profile data differs, transfers and state, effects and the evidence boundary. It is current at 009d40f5 except that the stock corpus is now shared with OPENGL4 and redundancy filtering is narrower than a general state cache. No retired renderer is discussed. The site already covered identity and profiles; the transfer, state, evidence-transfer and per-profile role material went to the EasyGL profiles deep dive.

concepts.text: EasyGL is the one current renderer family with several public identities: OPENGLES2, OPENGLES3, OPENGL33, WEBGL1 and WEBGL2, each with its own descriptor selecting a context and shader dialect; EASYGL itself is not a public selector.
The shared family centralises texture and buffer ownership, SpriteBatch, stock-effect programs, render targets, state translation and context-loss recovery.
tokens: The shared family owns texture and buffer resources

concepts.text: Runtime profile data selects the context request, GLSL dialect, format routes and limits, all through the GlProfile.hpp predicates (UsesGlslEs100, IsDesktopCoreProfile, UsesEs2ApiGeneration, RequiresBaseVertexPointerRebase).
Sharing does not erase API differences: the ES 2.0 generation lacks facilities of the others, and browser context loss and presentation differ from a desktop context.

The stock-effect corpus the family compiles is no longer EasyGL-private: at 009d40f5 it lives in the shared GlStockShaderSources.hpp and is also compiled by OPENGL4, so a stock-shader fix affects six identities in two families.
OPENGLES2 is the narrowest programmable profile; its ES 2.0-generation limits are pinned even on a newer context, and formats and instancing need explicit capability checks.
tokens: pinned even when the driver grants a newer context

concepts.text: OPENGLES3 is the default Linux profile and the principal native EasyGL evidence route, because the EasyGL suite registers only for a native EasyGL default renderer on non-Windows hosts.
OPENGL33 provides desktop 3.3 core through the EasyGL abstraction; it is the only profile with native base-vertex draws and is not OPENGL4.
tokens: the only profile that draws base-vertex ranges natively

concepts.text: WEBGL1 is the ES2-shaped browser route with web lifecycle constraints (Emscripten only).
WEBGL2 is the default Emscripten route and broader browser feature set; it is its own profile with no indexed colour masks, compute or indirect draw.
tokens: It is its own profile, not an alias

concepts.text: Uploads and render-target readback use format-aware GL paths plus CPU shadows where the public contract needs data the profile cannot recover; evidence must say which it observed, since a shadow round trip is not a driver readback.
tokens: a CPU-shadow round trip is not proof of a driver readback

concepts.text: Viewport and scissor are mapped through the active target's coordinate system, and texture-origin and presentation-origin conversions happen once at their owning boundary (bottom-up render targets, uRtFlipV, row reversal on readback, the shared presentation transform).
tokens: converted once, at the boundary that owns them

concepts.text: Redundant state is filtered where it matters: sampler parameters are shadowed per slot bit for bit, the GL viewport per context generation and the native polygon mode on change, and all shadows are cleared on context loss.
concepts.note: Older text described a general cache of blend, depth-stencil, rasterizer and sampler state; the verified redundancy filters are the sampler, viewport and polygon-mode shadows.

concepts.text: Cache correctness must be tested with state changes that visibly alter pixels; a counter-only test cannot show the driver received the intended values.
Stock effects compile renderer-owned GLSL variants from one ES 3.00 corpus adapted per profile to 330 core, ES 1.00 or ES 3.00.
ShaderEffect accepts the dialect the selected profile documents (GLSL ES on ES and WebGL, desktop GLSL on OPENGL33); it is not portable source.
Compiled XNA Effect Framework bytecode is an opt-in route owned by CNA_EASYGL_COMPILED_EFFECTS (default OFF, one switch for all five identities), not implied by choosing a GL identity.
The family has broad shared behavioural and pixel evidence, including SpriteBatch, stock effects, buffers, state, targets and the cross-renderer parity fixtures registered as EasyGL_Parity_*.

A result on one profile transfers to another only when the executed code and required feature are shared; base-vertex draws (native on OPENGL33, rebased elsewhere) and the ES 2.0 limits are concrete counter-examples.
tokens: transfers to another only when the executed code and the required feature are shared

concepts.text: Browser claims need a browser run: native EasyGL results do not prove the host-owned Emscripten loop or WebGL context behaviour, and the native suite registers no WebGL identity.
tokens: Browser claims additionally need a browser run
